# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S4 Add a `significantDigits` option to prettyBytes, with tests, docs, and types, following the earlier `unit` option work in the pretty-bytes repo (Nov 3, 6:06 AM)
**Investigated**: The `unit` option work from earlier in the session was reviewed, including its commits and the stale saved `unit: 'KB'` crash that prompted the no-throw rule for new options. The default 3-significant-digit rounding was traced to the no-locale-options branch of prettyBytes. The locale test expectations were checked against the new option, and the full npm test run was examined.

**Learned**: Default rounding to 3 significant digits lives in the no-locale-options branch of prettyBytes. Setting `minimumFractionDigits` or `maximumFractionDigits` causes `significantDigits` to be ignored. The integer part is never truncated, so `123` bytes with `significantDigits: 1` stays `123 B`. A value that rounds up into the next unit moves to that unit, so `999_900` with `significantDigits: 2` gives `1 MB`. Invalid values fall back to 3 without throwing.

**Completed**: The `significantDigits` helper was added to index.js, with invalid values (anything that is not an integer from 1 to 100) falling back to 3. The option is documented in readme.md and index.d.ts, and a type test was added to index.test-d.ts. test.js covers bigint, bits, locale, forced `unit`, fraction-option interaction, and invalid inputs. `npm test` passes with 53 passed and 3 skipped. Earlier, the `unit` option was committed as 32c1a03 and the bits-mode example as 654378b. The `significantDigits` changes are not yet committed.

**Next Steps**: Waiting on the user's decision about committing the significantDigits work. The 100 upper bound is a proposed cap that the user may want to lower.

**Notes**: The test.js edit changed one locale expectation to pair `significantDigits: 2` with `'1.337 kB'`, but the stated behavior is that `significantDigits: 2` yields `1.3 kB` and `4` yields `1.337 kB`. This mismatch should be checked before committing, because one of the two is likely wrong. The working tree currently has five modified files: index.d.ts, index.js, index.test-d.ts, readme.md, and test.js.
